criteria.reason: The exact-byte primitives hash correctly, but the callable Plan adapter returns an intent identity while RPI requires Plan to return raw bytes and mints again; the shared corpus does not compose Plan, Implement, RPI, a remote boundary, and Validate over one snapshot.
The dispatcher calls each phase at most once, emits every terminal report without continuation state, and preserves only the bounded opaque correlation object.
Repository-root before/final observation derives additions, modifications, deletions, mode/type changes, generated companions, incomplete coverage, and undeclared changes.
Frozen criterion IDs are exact and unique, required criteria cannot be excluded, and PASS requires evidence-backed coverage with no unchecked items.
The final subject is recomputed before and after judgment and any post-freeze mutation terminates validation.
Invocation and judgment identities are distinct and duplicate unlinked judgments sharing an invocation, judgment, or exact intent/final-subject pair are rejected.

The shared Python/Go corpus uses shallow case-specific outcome logic and does not drive strict readers for subject-manifest.v2, scope-index.v1, check-receipt.v1, effect-receipt.v1, or proof transition; Go strict readers exist only for verdict.v3 and rpi-report.v2.

The active pointer remains epoch 0b, the epoch-1 descriptor binds every component and recorder to exact subject bytes and modes, bootstrap qualification is external, and the general recorder enforces prior-proof PASS, membership, content-addressed transition bytes, CAS, and active-pointer-last ordering.
Both Python and Go explicitly accept the raw dot repository reference instead of rejecting it lexically, and no production command or call site atomically writes a named check-receipt artifact.

findings.summary: The shipped Plan adapter and RPI dispatcher expose incompatible Plan result shapes, and the shared corpus does not compose an exact snapshot through the required remote boundary.
The shared Python/Go corpus does not exercise strict readers for five of the required typed proof surfaces.
A raw dot repository reference is accepted and resolves to the repository root in both candidate implementations.
The kernel can construct a check receipt in memory but exposes no callable named atomic output writer for it.
